findings.problem: status: String is a primitive lifecycle flag. Any arbitrary string value ("", "deleted", "sent", "SENT") is valid, making illegal states representable and unenforceable by the compiler.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can construct LedgerWorkflow with status="foo" or status="" and no code path can reject it at compile time; runtime logic must string-compare against magic literals everywhere.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with an enum typestate, e.g. `pub enum LedgerStatus { New, Validated, Sent }` and make invalid transitions constructors reject them.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a primitive lifecycle flag orthogonal to status: String. The struct can hold status="new" with is_validated=true, which is an illegal state with no invariant enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: Business logic that checks `is_validated` to gate downstream actions runs on a field whose value can diverge from `status`, causing silent authorization bypasses or duplicate validation.
findings.fix: Fold validation into the enum typestate so the compiler forbids invalid combinations (e.g., `LedgerStatus::Validated` carries the validation invariant).

findings.problem: is_sent: bool is a primitive lifecycle flag orthogonal to status: String. The struct can hold status="sent" with is_sent=false or status="new" with is_sent=true.
findings.failure_mode: Divergent state between `status` and `is_sent` causes callers checking one field but not the other to make incorrect decisions (double-sending or missed sends).
findings.fix: Eliminate `is_sent` entirely; encode sent state in the enum typestate. Store sent_at_epoch_ms only in the Sent variant.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain newtype. Any string (empty, " ", malformed UUIDs) is accepted with no compile-time guarantee of validity.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code must re-parse or re-validate the ID on every access; empty IDs slip through silently.
findings.fix: Introduce a `LedgerId` newtype with a fallible constructor that validates the ID format at the boundary. The struct field becomes `pub id: LedgerId`.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs `.to_string()` allocation on every call, which is a heap allocation in what should be a pure, deterministic core function. The function is labeled as a pure transformation but allocates on the hot path.
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded allocation on a pure-function hot path defeats zero-cost abstraction expectations and causes unpredictable GC/allocator pressure.
findings.fix: Replace `item.status = "sent".to_string()` with an enum assignment (zero allocation). If the enum carries `sent_at_epoch_ms`, use the variant constructor directly.

findings.problem: mark_sent sets both `status = "sent"` and `is_sent = true`, duplicating state that represents the same domain fact. This is the anti-pattern that makes illegal states possible.
findings.failure_mode: A partial update (e.g., setting one field but not the other via struct update syntax or a bug) leaves the struct in a self-contradictory state that no single boolean or string check can detect.
findings.fix: Use a single enum typestate so the domain fact "sent" is represented exactly once. The function becomes a pure transition: `LedgerWorkflow -> Result<LedgerWorkflow, TransitionError>`.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes any LedgerWorkflow regardless of its current state. It can be called on a workflow that is already sent, never validated, or in any other state, with no precondition check.
findings.failure_mode: Domain invariants are violated at runtime (e.g., sending an unvalidated ledger). Errors are silently ignored instead of being surfaced to the caller.
findings.fix: Change the signature to `pub fn mark_sent(item: &LedgerWorkflow) -> Result<LedgerWorkflow, TransitionError>` and validate the pre-condition (e.g., must be Validated) before transitioning.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent hot-path performance
no profiler data to quantify .to_string() allocation frequency on the hot path
no allocation tracing evidence (e.g., heaptrack/valgrind) for the current implementation
no second-ring evidence (assembly/allocator) proving the enum refactor eliminates heap allocation
no command-level evidence (cargo bench / cargo asm) for any stated performance claim
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has fundamental typestate violations that make illegal states representable at compile time. The functional core is contaminated with I/O-adjacent allocations (.to_string()). All 7 findings are BLOCKER severity — the crate requires structural repair (enum typestate, domain newtypes, fallible transitions) before it can pass Holzman gates. No benchmark or profiler evidence exists to validate any performance claim.
